name: snapshot_chain_check
description: Read the descriptors and headers of virtual-disk files and say how they chain: which file names which as its parent, whether the parent is in the set, whether the identity the child recorded is the identity the parent carries, which extents a descriptor needs and which are missing or short, and which markers a consolidation or an unclean close may leave. It reads, from their public descriptions and no others: VMware VMDK (a text descriptor, or the descriptor embedded in a sparse extent, versions 1 to 3; CID and parentCID as the 1 to 8 hexadecimal digits a writer prints, compared as numbers; parentFileNameHint, createType, extents; a COWD extent is recognised and not read), .vmx and .vmsd (only the disk file names and the snapshot database), VHD (footer, dynamic header, parent unique id, name and locators, with the checksums), VHDX (both headers with CRC-32C and sequence, region table, metadata, file parameters, virtual disk id, parent locator; a child's parent_linkage is held against the parent's DataWriteGuid of its current header, as MS-VHDX says it records, and the virtual disk id is information) and QCOW2 versions 2 and 3 (header, backing file and format, feature bits, header extensions, the internal snapshot table, streamed). A name inside a file is looked up among the files given and never opened by the tool; a parent outside the set is reported missing. It reads headers and descriptors, not disk content: a chain it calls complete has every named parent in the set and read, agreeing identities where the format records one (QCOW2 records none of its backing file, so only its name links it, and a raw backing file is a base that is present and not read), and every extent and external data file in the set; any other chain names the first problem from its leaf (cycle, too_deep, broken, record_incomplete, parent_unreadable, identity_not_compared, identity_mismatch, extent_missing, data_file_missing) and lists every kind found. It is not a disk that boots or a statement about what the parent held when the child was made. A marker (an unclean-shutdown flag, a QCOW2 dirty bit, a VHDX log GUID, a delta no snapshot or configuration names, a running disk that is a delta while the snapshot database lists none, a lock artefact, an identity mismatch, two descriptors with one CID, parent names that disagree, an absent external data file) is a candidate with its observation beside it, never a verdict. The layouts are implemented from the format descriptions and are checked here against synthetic files; they have not been checked against files made by every product or version, and a version the tool does not know is reported and not read. Nothing is mounted, converted, repaired, merged or executed. Chains are found without recursion in one memoised pass, with a depth cap, cycle detection (a cycle no leaf reaches has a chain row of its own) and the clock checked throughout; a descriptor is read to 1 MiB, a .vmx or .vmsd over 16 MiB is named and not read, a .vmsd lists at most 20000 snapshot indexes (the rest are counted), and a QCOW2 snapshot table read short of its declared count is partial. A Hyper-V header that fails its own check (a VHD footer or dynamic-header checksum, both VHDX headers' or both region tables' CRC-32C; of the two region-table copies the first that holds is read) is read as written, named by a marker and makes the answer partial, and so does one VHDX header that fails its signature or CRC-32C (the other is taken as current) and a VHD whose end footer is missing (the start copy is read); a QCOW2 child that declares a qcow2 backing format over a raw file is parent_unreadable; and so does a chain the max_chain_depth limit stopped. A chain over a descriptor or header the tool did not read whole is record_incomplete, never complete: a descriptor of more than 20000 lines or 1 MiB (also one embedded in a sparse extent), an extent line in a shape it cannot read (RW, RDONLY or NOACCESS with a name that is not quoted, a lower-case keyword, a negative size, a trailing token), a descriptor with no extent line, a CID or parentCID that is not a number, a parentCID with no parentFileNameHint, a QCOW2 backing file name outside the file or over 1023 bytes, more than 64 header extensions, an extension that runs past the first cluster, or the external-data-file bit set with no name; the file is partial too. A .vmx or .vmsd line over 64 KiB, or past line 500000, is not read: the file is partial and the first such line is named. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`, the pair the recipes' coverage.json carries; exit 0 means the engine ran, not that the examination is complete. SENSITIVE: every string the answer shows is judged by the field it fills, in three layers, with the boundary text that the Windows and macOS tools carry too (one text in all 16 carriers). (1) A name (VM, datastore, snapshot, storage, key), a path or file name, an identifier (GUID, VMFS volume id, naa./eui./t10./wwn- device id, VMware uuid, MAC, CID, number) and a simple value (an enum word, a version, a time) is shown only when it fits the plain grammar of its kind: letters of any script, digits, space and a short list of punctuation, at most 128 characters a name (a path is judged component by component), no user-info shape, no secret's name beside a value, and no chain of 16 or more characters made of random-looking pieces (a GUID, a hexadecimal id of up to 24 digits, a number of up to 18 digits and the well-formed ids of devices are plain; an iqn. or t10. id is shown as an id only when what it holds reads as a name, and a t10. serial of 17 or more hexadecimal digits is withheld); anything else is `<withheld N characters: reason>` (a path component by component), and its original goes to the values files only with write_text in a job. (2) Every other text (a host name, a description, an annotation, an audit action or actor, a message) is judged on a copy with invisible and formatting characters taken out and the escapes of such characters decoded: user-info up to the last `@`, token-shaped runs, prefixed tokens (ghp_, AKIA, glpat-, sk_live_, SG., AIza and others), a PEM key, a run of more than 18 digits, and the value after a name that says it is a secret (password, passwd, passphrase, pwd, secret, token, credential, api, access, account or private key, auth, pw, sig, sas, otp, psk; any case, glued or CamelCase) after `=` or `:`, after a flag that takes one (-password x, --token x, --api-key x, -auth x, set password x, enable secret x) and behind a placeholder (password=<redacted>x, or <redacted> x when x is built like a secret), in time linear in the length; a name or a path component that holds a secret's name and, glued or after a space, a value of 7 or more characters built like a secret (password-Zq7kP2mR, Token Zq7kP2mR) is withheld whole. In free text these shapes are still shown whole (2,000 random plants per shape, two samples of 1,000 with different seeds, with 95% Wilson bounds in the pack's changelog): `password-srv01-` and 8 characters, 100% in each of seven alphabets (at least 99.8%); with 14 base62 characters 63%, with 24 0.05%; `password-` and two groups of 4 characters, 100%; a glued `--master-key` and 8 lower-case letters 7.7%, 8 hexadecimal digits 0.8%, 8 base62 characters 0.2%, 14 or 24 base62 characters none in 2,000. (3) The serialised answer, every error answer and every paging-file row are read back and checked by a second check written apart from the first two; a string it finds suspect, or in which it finds a piece of a secret-shaped text that the first two left between two cuts, is replaced by <withheld N bytes: backstop: why>, its place is listed in boundary.replaced_at, and the answer is partial. The judging of one run shares a cap of 400 million characters and a time that ends 6.5 seconds after max_seconds: past either, a string not judged before is withheld by its size (a short plain word stays readable), the answer is partial and boundary.stopped_by names the stop. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP that arrives once the module has run as far as its shared opening blocks (before any argument is read and before any evidence is touched) ends the tool with one JSON answer (status partial, stopped_by_signal naming the signal) and exit status 128 plus the signal number; one that arrives earlier, while the interpreter starts and compiles the file and runs those blocks, gets no answer. Only the exact names of the files this run made are shown as they are; an extension that is not 1 to 10 letters or digits is counted under (other extensions). A short password used as a name, a token under 16 characters in a name, a value of 6 characters or fewer after a secret's name, a value built like words, a name the grammar of a plain name refuses (it is withheld: a false positive), and the shapes listed with their measured rates in the pack's changelog are not recognised, so run as a job with secret_output: true. write_text: true (refused outside a job) creates two files under $OUT, mode 0600, both created before anything is read: chain-values.jsonl (the original of every name or value shown withheld or shortened) and snapshot_chain_check-values.jsonl (the original of every string the boundary withheld or replaced, one JSON line each: id, field, label, length, value); a file already there is refused by name.  A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 10: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

root.description: A directory of the evidence files (a link is refused; links inside it are listed and never followed). Give root, paths, or both

paths.description: Files named one by one (a link or a special file is named and never opened)

limit.description: Rows shown inline per list (default 200); every row is counted and, when there are more, the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results; the rows shown inline also stop at about 512 KiB per list whatever limit says (pages.<list>.inline_cut_by_size), so that the answer is written within max_seconds and keeps its status: the rest is in the file

max_files.description: The most files taken into the set (default 20000, at most 200000); past it the answer is partial and says where the walk stopped

max_entries.description: The most directory entries listed (default 200000, at most 2000000)

max_depth.description: How deep the walk goes (default 16, at most 64); a deeper directory is named

max_seconds.description: The time to spend (default 50, at most 50); what is left is named and the answer is partial; the reading stops at four fifths of it and the rest is kept for writing the rows and the answer, which stop at max_seconds itself (a stop is named in partial_reasons)

write_text.description: Write the original of every name or value the answer shows withheld or shortened to 0600 files under $OUT (the tool's own text file and snapshot_chain_check-values.jsonl) (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job that is secret output: the manifest declares it, so a job with write_text true is made secret by the job service whether or not the agent asked

max_snapshots.description: The most internal QCOW2 snapshots read from one image (default 100000); the declared count is kept beside the number read

max_chain_depth.description: The longest chain followed (default 10000); a longer one is reported as too deep

qemu_img.description: off (default), auto or require. auto runs `qemu-img info --output=json -f <format> <image>` once per parsed image of the set (never --backing-chain), when qemu-img is on PATH; require fails when it is not. A VMDK text descriptor, a sparse VMDK of capacity 0 or whose embedded descriptor names a file other than itself, and a QCOW2 image with an external data file are not given to it (qemu-img would open the files they name), nor an extent another descriptor names; a run that fails, times out or prints no JSON, and an eligible image left unchecked at qemu_img_max_images or the clock, make the answer partial. Its answer sits beside the native reading and replaces nothing

qemu_img_max_images.description: The most images qemu-img is run on (default 50)
